language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi. I am Tom! I am aboard a ship on the Atlantic ocean with my dad. He is doing research on the Titanic shipwreck. Exciting, isn't it?
When I grow up, I want to be a weather man who forecasts weather accurately so that less ships get shipwrecked. Won’t that be great?
Here’s the first thing I’m trying to figure out. I want to measure the wind speed. Which apparatus should I look at?
Well… the 'anemometer' will be able to help!

I came across these weather forecasts for the days to come, at sea. Can you help me match the weather forecasts to the corresponding diagrams?

helperSimple.text: Match each forecast to the correct weather diagram.

outro.text: Thanks a ton. Now I know how to better understand weather forecasts!

activities.title: What does it measure? Click on the correct answer.

These instruments are a wind vane and a windsock.
They can turn to any direction.

I met my father’s friends who are sailors. I heard them ask on what day they should set sail from the harbor. I know about the weather predictions for next week. Can you help me figure out the answers?

helperSimple.text: Select the best day for setting sail.

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Uncle Leon says 'I don't like setting sail on a day when rains are predicted.' What day should he NOT set sail?

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Uncle Fan says 'I will prefer a bright, clear, but not too sunny a day to set sail.' What day should he set sail?

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Uncle Tim says 'My boat only has sails. It needs help from the wind to travel out of the harbor.' What day should he set sail?

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: Uncle Peter says 'I like to set sail from harbor on a clear and sunny day.' What day should he set sail?

activities.title: Click on the correct answer.
activities.subtitle: My father says that no ships should set sail on a day when visibility is Iow. What day should none of his sailor friends set sail?

outro.text: Wow! Now I can start advising sailors too!
